evidence: holistic_context.authorization: empty — static analysis found no auth patterns to report
The codebase is a multi-language active inference simulation demo with no web framework, no route handlers, no database, no user sessions, and no permission system of any kind

run_all.sh, status_dashboard.sh, Shell/config.sh, Shell/Active_Shellference.sh, Shell/run.sh: all are local shell scripts that operate on the filesystem; they do not accept user-supplied input over a network, do not authenticate callers, and do not manage user sessions
Shell/run.sh lines 22-38: creates files and chmod +x — these are local filesystem operations run by whoever invokes the script; there is no multi-user trust boundary to enforce
Python/Student_Teacher.py: no HTTP endpoints, no user input beyond matplotlib output directory; no auth surface
TypeScript/src/ActiveInferenceAgent.ts: no HTTP handlers, no route decorators, no permission checks needed
No database access, no SQL, no RLS, no service roles, no admin bypasses in any of the reviewed files
SQL/ directory exists but contains a demo simulation stored procedure, not user-facing data access with row-level security concerns
authorization_consistency.issues_preventing_higher_score: Shell scripts use `chmod +x` and `find ... -exec chmod +x` globally on all run.sh files without scoping to known-safe files — this is a minor permission hygiene concern, not a multi-user auth gap, but it is the only authorization-adjacent pattern in the codebase

strengths: No web endpoints, route handlers, or user-facing APIs exist, so there is no surface area for inconsistent auth decoration
No database access patterns to audit for RLS coverage
No permission strings or role constants in any file, eliminating the magic-literal permission risk
authorization_consistency.issue_character: The codebase has no authorization surface at all — it is a local simulation demo; the only authorization-adjacent behavior is filesystem permission changes in shell scripts, which are applied consistently.
authorization_consistency.score_rationale: This dimension does not apply meaningfully to the codebase as reviewed: there are no network-accessible endpoints, no user sessions, no permission systems, and no multi-tenant data boundaries. The score of 88 reflects that what little authorization-adjacent behavior exists (chmod operations in shell scripts) is consistently applied, while the small deduction acknowledges that run_all.sh uses `find . -name run.sh -exec chmod +x {} \;` which applies executable permissions broadly without filtering to known-safe locations — a minor hardening gap rather than a real auth vulnerability.

issues.summary: run_all.sh applies chmod +x to all run.sh files recursively without scoping to known-safe directories
evidence: Line 177: find . -name "run.sh" -type f -exec chmod +x {} \; — marks every file named run.sh under the repo root as executable, including any run.sh files introduced by external tools or cloned submodules
issues.suggestion: Scope the chmod to known language directories only: `for lang_info in "${LANGUAGES[@]}"; do lang_dir="${lang_info#*:}"; [ -f "$lang_dir/run.sh" ] && chmod +x "$lang_dir/run.sh"; done` — this applies executable permissions only to the 39 known language scripts

root_causes: This codebase is a local-execution simulation demo and inherently has no multi-user auth surface; scoring this dimension is largely N/A
